knowledge_base.title: Dental Care FAQ
knowledge_base.content:
Q: How often should I visit the dentist?
A: We recommend a dental checkup and cleaning every 6 months for most patients. Those with gum disease may need more frequent visits.

Q: Does teeth cleaning hurt?
A: Professional cleaning is generally painless. You may feel slight sensitivity during scaling, but our team ensures your comfort throughout.

Q: How long does a root canal take?
A: A root canal typically takes 1-2 visits, each lasting about 60-90 minutes depending on the tooth.

Q: Do you accept insurance?
A: Yes, we work with most major dental insurance providers. Please bring your insurance card to your first visit.

Q: What should I do in a dental emergency?
A: For severe pain, swelling, or a knocked-out tooth, call our emergency number immediately. For a knocked-out tooth, keep it moist in milk and come in within 30 minutes.

knowledge_base.title: Pre-Procedure Instructions
knowledge_base.content:
Before Your Dental Appointment:
- Brush and floss your teeth before your visit
- Arrive 15 minutes early for paperwork if you're a new patient
- Inform us of any medications you're taking
- Let us know if you have any allergies
- If you feel anxious, let us know - we offer sedation options

After a Dental Procedure:
- Avoid eating until numbness wears off (usually 2-3 hours)
- Take prescribed medications as directed
- Apply ice for swelling (20 minutes on, 20 minutes off)
- Stick to soft foods for 24-48 hours after extractions
- Call us if you experience severe pain or prolonged bleeding
